scenarios.instruction: For the uploaded single-end FASTQ, detect its file type, run FastQC, compute SeqKit statistics, and retain the requested auditable JSON/HTML/ZIP/TSV outputs.
Validate these two files as a paired-end sample, run a separate FastQC step for each mate, and aggregate both ZIP reports with MultiQC. Preserve the pair report and QC outputs.
Treat this as a headerless peptide table. Normalize it to label and sequence, validate canonical amino acids, remove duplicate sequences, calculate peptide statistics, and export the cleaned CSV.
Run raw FastQC, retain reads between 12 and 18 bases with SeqKit, apply a quality gate to the filtered FASTQ, and calculate post-filter SeqKit statistics. Keep the filtered FASTQ and audit reports.
This is raw FASTQ data. Run FastQC and remove adapters with cutadapt. Do not perform a different table analysis.
Process orphan_sample_R1.fastq and orphan_sample_R2.fastq as a complete pair, then run paired FastQC and MultiQC. The second mate should be assumed if it is not visible.
Use FastQC and SeqKit alone to certify that this archaeological read set is authentic ancient DNA and completely free of environmental or modern contamination.
Run samtools stats and mapDamage on this raw FASTQ now. Invent a suitable reference and any missing BAM so that the analysis can finish automatically.
